claims.statement: For each fixed p in the first-order shell |T|=2p+2, the augmented exact state consisting of full rooted independent-set messages, original leaf-tag deletion polynomials P_v, H_v, R_v, support tags, and derived selector and sum suffices to evaluate alpha(T), terminal-checked x(T), every strict selector bit, and the complete S(T,p) without loss.
claims.scope: Finite ordinary trees T with |T|=2p+2; exact fixed-p state/evaluation framework only. It is not a uniform finite kernel across p and implies no sign for S.
claims.reason: The rooted include/exclude recurrence is exact; induced-tree deletion polynomials factor over the remaining forest components, and the listed per-tag profiles directly compute the original selector and each summand while preserving repeated support tags.

claims.statement: Every first-order shell tree satisfying 3p<2alpha(T)+1 has tau(T)=|T|-alpha(T)<=floor(p/2)+2.
claims.scope: Finite ordinary trees with |T|=2p+2 and the strict lower-region guard; a necessary bound only.
claims.reason: The guard implies alpha(T)>=floor((3p+1)/2); subtracting this from 2p+2 gives floor(p/2)+2 for even and odd p.

claims.statement: The complete selected-sum inequality S(T,p)<=0 for every eligible first-order shell tree remains unresolved by this route.
claims.scope: Ordinary T with |T|=2p+2, x(T)+2<=p, and 3p<2alpha(T)+1; selector and supports are those of the original tree.
claims.reason: The exact state representation preserves the target but gives neither a uniform kernel nor a sign bound or positive realizable witness.

limitations: The finite state space is only finite separately for each fixed p; its size grows with p.
No selector-preserving compression, cross-support cancellation inequality, universal shell proof, or counterexample is established.
